newsitem.title: CHINA: Bank of China to issue overseas bonds this year.
newsitem.headline: Bank of China to issue overseas bonds this year.

text.p: China's financial institutions expect to increase issues of overseas bonds this year, with the State Development Bank set to launch $350 million in Yankee bonds and the Bank of China also planning an issue.

Funds raised from the bond issues will be used in key projects, such as power plants and steel, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday, quoting an official of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE).
Domestic financial institutions were being encouraged to turn to international capital markets to raise funds, he said.
Domestic financial institutions last year issued nine batches of bonds abroad, raising $1.81 billion, and the amount was expected to increase this year, the newspaper said.

The State Development Bank, which finances major infrastructure profects in China, had approval to issue $350 million worth of bonds in the United States in the near future, it said. It gave no details of the issue.
The state-owned commercial Bank of China planned to issue overseas bonds this year after a two-year absence from the market, it said.
The three other state banks, the China Construction Bank, the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China and the Agricultural Bank of China also planned to issue bonds overseas in 1997, it said.
